name: Safety vs Functionality
title: Safety vs Functionality
description: A system can work perfectly and still be unsafe: the elevator that moves smoothly but ignores the door sensor. Safety verification checks safety properties specifically, beyond functional correctness.
how_it_works: Define safety properties separately from functional requirements (what must never happen, what must always happen), and verify them with dedicated methods. Functional tests passing does not imply safety.
requirements: Identified hazards with safety requirements; defined safe states; independent verification resources.
standards: Functional safety standards: IEC 61508, ISO 26262 (automotive), DO-178C/DO-254 (aviation), IEC 62304 (medical).
citations: IEC 61508 functional safety of electrical/electronic systems.
ISO 26262 road vehicles - functional safety.

name: Safe States
title: Safe States
description: A safe state is where the system rests without causing harm when faults occur: motors stopped, outputs de-energized, valves closed. Every safety design defines its safe states.
how_it_works: Define safe states for each operating mode, design fault responses to reach them, and verify the transitions under injected faults. Safe states must be reachable from every fault considered.
key_points: Fault responses drive to safe states.
requirements: Identified hazards with safety requirements; defined safe states; independent verification resources.
